content.text: {"similarities":["Both show a soft, blob-like head with a face, with a tilted rectangular power strip rising from its top in place of a normal crown.","In both, the strip leans to the upper right and carries two stacked outlets, each with two vertical slots above a round hole.","In both, a cord leaves the top end of the strip, arcs up and over to the left, and comes back down to end in a thickened plug at the top of the head beside the base of the strip. The strip therefore appears looped back into the figure itself.","In both, the strip blends into the head through a tapering neck-like transition rather than sitting on it as a separate object.","Both faces sit low and right of centre on the blob and have two eyes with brow marks above them, a nose and a mouth, with vertical streams running down the lower face.","Both have a bulging mass on the left of the head, a wider flaring lower part like shoulders or a bust, and a small zigzag mark near the bottom centre."],"differences":[{"observation":"The streams start at the eyes in the drawing but at the mouth or chin in the sculpture.","evidence":"In Image 1, blue lines begin at the lower edge of each eye and run down the cheeks. In Images 2 and 3, the rod-like strands with rounded drop ends hang from a blob at the lower lip, and nothing runs down from the ring-shaped eyes."},{"observation":"The mouth is a small closed line in the drawing but a large, open, protruding form in the sculpture.","evidence":"Image 1 has a short downturned stroke under the nose. Images 2 and 3 show a raised upper lip, a recess with a small peg-like element, and a bulging lower mass; the side view shows it projecting from the surface."},{"observation":"The eyes and brows are drawn differently.","evidence":"Image 1 has angular, slanted eyes with a filled dark pupil in the left one and brow lines pinched toward the nose. Images 2 and 3 have round ring-shaped eyes with hollow centres and separate straight bar-like brows."},{"observation":"The nose is a line in the drawing and a separate protruding knob in the sculpture.","evidence":"In Image 1, the nose is a stroke continuous with the right eye and brow. In Images 2 and 3, a distinct raised nose with a rounded tip sits between and below the eyes and stands out in profile."},{"observation":"The face is larger relative to the head in the sculpture.","evidence":"In Image 1, the features form a small cluster low on the blob with a lot of blank area around them. In Image 2, the brows, eyes, nose, mouth and strands span much of the head's width and height."},{"observation":"The plug is more defined in the drawing and more generalised in the sculpture.","evidence":"Image 1 shows a blocky plug body with a collar band where the cord enters, its tip meeting the outline where strip and head join. Images 2 and 3 show a smooth spindle-shaped swelling that fuses into the top of the head just left of the strip base, with no collar or flat face."},{"observation":"The cord's exit from the strip is ribbed in the drawing and smooth in the sculpture.","evidence":"Image 1 has several short cross lines at the top of the strip where the cord emerges. Images 2 and 3 have a smooth rounded collar there."},{"observation":"The outlets are framed differently.","evidence":"In Image 1, each outlet is a rounded outline on the strip's front face, and a long line down the strip separates a narrow side face. In Images 2 and 3, each outlet sits in a square recessed frame on a plain box with flat sides."},{"observation":"The head and lower body have different proportions and boundaries.","evidence":"In Image 1, the right side of the head drops fairly smoothly and the bottom outlines run off to the left and right, leaving the lower body open. In Images 2 and 3, the head bulges on both sides, pinches to a neck, and sits on a closed dome-like base with a flat bottom."},{"observation":"Interior lines in the drawing appear as grooves in different positions on the sculpture.","evidence":"Image 1 has one long diagonal contour from the left of the head down toward the lower right, plus a small squiggle at the bottom. Image 2 has a short dashed diagonal groove left of the mouth, a bent groove at the lower left, short marks near the strands, and a larger W-shaped zigzag."},{"observation":"The drawing uses colour for the streams and the sculpture has none.","evidence":"The streams in Image 1 are blue against black line work. Images 2 and 3 are uniform light grey."}],"interpretation":"Both depictions show the same basic idea: a crying or distressed blob-headed character whose head extends into a two-outlet power strip, with the strip's cord looping back to plug in at the top of the head. The overall arrangement and the cord, strip and head connections match closely. The main difference in content is the face. The drawing reads as crying, with tears from the eyes and a small frown. The sculpture's strands hang from an open, protruding mouth, which I infer reads more as drooling or something spilling from the mouth, alongside rounder eyes and a more prominent nose. The other differences are in detailing (plug, strain relief, outlet framing), proportions, and how the open-ended lower body in the drawing becomes a closed bust-like base.","uncertainty":["In the drawing it is unclear whether the plug enters the head or the lower side of the strip, because its tip sits right at the junction of the two outlines.","The sculpture's strands could be drool, a tongue with drips, or displaced tears; the views cannot settle which.","The small peg inside the sculpture's mouth could be a tooth or a modelling artefact.","Matching the sculpture's grooves to specific lines in the drawing (neck contour, shoulder line, bottom squiggle) is my inference.","Only two views of the sculpture are provided, so its back and far side are not visible.","The drawing is flat, so the depth of its features and the strip's thickness can only be inferred."]}
